top.line: A line in every project budget for maintaining its core platforms, sized to the project and delivering every month; four weeks of php2shell data show what is missing without it.
top.para: The proposal, and the NCSC-NL inventory four weeks after php2shell: 976 entries, 218 with a fix, 214 not vulnerable, but 211 still marked vulnerable (221 on 23 October), 240 runtime-dependent and 92 with no answer.

in-short.line: A cost item, a named risk when missing, proportional, monthly, reaching the maintainers, affordable with Gen AI, and mappable now.
in-short.para: Seven points on the line and the data.

proposal.line: Platform maintenance belongs in each project's own budget, proportional to its spend and delivering all the time; its absence is a named risk.
proposal.para: From Dinis's comment of 24 October: not a central or charity budget, but a line beside hosting and testing, small and many, and never seen as insurance.

data.line: The NCSC-NL inventory went from 749 to 976 entries; fixes doubled to 218, but vulnerable entries barely moved, 221 to 211.
data.para: Weekly counts from the inventory's git history, matching its own statistics; under investigation fell mostly by reclassification into the new runtime-dependent status.

missing.line: 543 entries lack a fix or a clean status: 211 vulnerable, 240 runtime-dependent, 92 unanswered, each a way nobody was paid to know.
missing.para: The three kinds, what each means for an organisation, and how any organisation can build the same map for its own projects as its risk register.

the-line.line: The line names the platform, who maintains it, its share of spend, what it delivers each month, the evidence, and the risk when absent.
the-line.para: No share is proposed; what matters is that the line is proportional and recurring, so it moves with the project.

compared.line: The Open Source Pledge, foundation sponsorship and LTS vendors all move money, but none is a per-project line for the platform it runs.
compared.para: The Pledge asks over $2,000 a year per employed developer; sponsorship buys recognition; vendors sell patched builds. The line is sized to the project and buys work on its exact platform.

chain.line: Maintainers are paid to help set up and maintain what is built on top, and each step pays the one below.
chain.para: Money comes with work, and quality is pushed down the chain.

gen-ai.line: Gen AI makes small lines buy real work by helping people understand code, side effects and changes, not by writing all the code.
gen-ai.para: The maintainers' judgement is what the line pays for.

interest.line: RiskMandate is open source, starts at £0, paid help from £500; the argument does not depend on who sells the work.

limits.line: A proposal; no share proposed; entries not organisations; labels changed; inventory incomplete; no compromise claimed; my interest.

sources.line: Dinis's comment of 24 October; the NCSC-NL php2shell repository at five commits; the Open Source Pledge; earlier articles here.
sources.para: Counts by newsroom.d (writer-11), checked against the inventory's statistics file.
